items.title: Jimmy Owens interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: And I remember that time that Johnny Gary told Pee Wee Marquette, okay let him in. For free.

ctx.x: That’s great. Did the musicians that you met, either as teachers or just in the clubs, did you get a sense of them instilling you with other things, just besides the playing of the music? © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

Well I can’t say — I mentioned that Donald Byrd was my mentor. And he instilled in me what being a professional musician was. He taught me about the business. He was the first to start that, let’s put it that way. And made me aware about copyright, and about taking care of business. And then there were other musicians who were equally as important and took it another step. Randy Weston was one of my mentors also.
